questions.question: What are the basics of React Router v6?
questions.title: React Router v6 Basics — Routes, Route, Link, useNavigate
questions.direct_answer:
What are the basics of React Router v6?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** BrowserRouter, Routes, Route element prop, nested routes, Outlet, Link/NavLink, useNavigate, useParams.

**Classic weak answer:** Still writing component-prop syntax (v5 style) — v6 uses the element prop and auto-relative nested routes.

**Senior finish:** Highlight v6 breaking changes vs v5, the new data routers (createBrowserRouter), and loaders/actions.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **React Router v6 Basics — Routes, Route, Link, useNavigate** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What are the basics of React Router v6?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **BrowserRouter, Routes, Route element prop, nested routes, Outlet, Link/NavLink, useNavigate, useParams**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still writing component-prop syntax (v5 style) — v6 uses the element prop and auto-relative nested routes**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Highlight v6 breaking changes vs v5, the new data routers (createBrowserRouter), and loaders/actions**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** BrowserRouter, Routes, Route element prop, nested routes, Outlet, Link/NavLink, useNavigate, useParams
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

```mermaid
    COMMIT --> EF[useEffect after paint]

    DIFF --> MEMO
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **still writing component-prop syntax (v5 style) — v6 uses the element prop and auto-relative nested routes** and what you do instead.

questions.question: What do useParams, useSearchParams, and useLocation do in React Router?
questions.title: useParams, useSearchParams & useLocation — React Router Hooks
questions.direct_answer:
What do useParams, useSearchParams, and useLocation do in React Router?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** useParams: URL path params; useSearchParams: query string (get/set tuple); useLocation: full location (pathname, search, hash, state).

**Classic weak answer:** Mutating searchParams.get result directly — useSearchParams returns a tuple [params, setParams]; use setParams to update.

**Senior finish:** Show typical patterns: filters in URL via useSearchParams, scroll-restoration with useLocation.
